clues.title: Coverage: coastal region next to a big mainland
text: Hong Kong is located in Southern China, sharing a border with the Guangdong province. It is a Chinese **Special Administrative Region**, so for country streaks purposes, it is counted as part of China.
_You can click on the image to enlarge it._
clues.summary: A special region in southern China, bordering Guangdong province. For country streaks it counts as China.

clues.title: Plate: white front, yellow rear
text: Hong Kong has **white **front licence plates and **yellow **rear** **licence plates. The licence plates can be long or short. Some cars have an additional [black](https://maps.app.goo.gl/cyTzqwmo1qrNYJxZ9) mainland Chinese licence plate.
clues.summary: White front plates and yellow rear plates, long or short. Some cars carry an extra black mainland Chinese plate.

clues.title: Driving side: left
text: Hong Kong drives on the **left**.
NOTE: Singapore also drives on the left, however Taiwan drives on the right.

images.caption: A Hong Kong road with traffic driving on the left; the added sign shows two-way traffic

clues.summary: Traffic drives on the left. Singapore also drives on the left, but Taiwan drives on the right.

clues.title: Houses: dense skyscraper city, busy streets
text: Hong Kong is a densely populated city with millions of inhabitants. In urban areas, modern **skyscrapers **are common, with **busy** streets filled with vehicles and pedestrians.
The city has a unique vibe that you can quickly pick up on. In many cases, this vibe alone should be sufficient to identify urban Hong Kong locations.
clues.summary: Modern skyscrapers and busy streets full of cars and people. The city feel alone usually identifies urban areas.

clues.title: Landscape: green mountains, tall blocks nearby
text: There is also a plethora of rural locations that are harder to identify.

Outside the urban areas, Hong Kong is generally quite **mountainous**, with green, subtropical vegetation. There is extensive coverage in rural areas outside the city, with many roads going through the mountains. You might see low-rise rural buildings, however usually you will not need to travel far to see tall apartment blocks.
NOTE: Singapore, on the other hand, is very flat.
clues.summary: Outside the city it is mountainous with green subtropical plants and lots of rural roads. Tall apartment blocks are almost always close. Singapore is very flat.

clues.title: Houses: extremely tall apartment blocks
text: One very striking aspect of Hong Kong architecture are the many extremely **tall apartment buildings** found throughout the city.
NOTE: Apartment buildings in Singapore and Taiwan tend to be not nearly as tall as those in Hong Kong.
clues.summary: Very tall apartment buildings all over the city, much taller than in Singapore or Taiwan.

clues.title: Houses: wall-mounted air conditioners
text: Because of the subtropical climate,** air conditioners** attached to the walls of apartments are very common in Hong Kong.
clues.summary: Air conditioners bolted to apartment walls are very common because of the subtropical climate.

clues.title: Language: English and traditional Chinese
text: Hong Kong has two official languages: **English and Chinese** (legally, no variety is specified, but residents primarily speak Cantonese).
Bilingual signs are common, with English next to traditional Chinese characters.

images.caption: Hong Kong street scenes with English and traditional Chinese signs

clues.summary: English sits next to traditional Chinese characters on bilingual signs. People mostly speak Cantonese.

clues.title: Pole: grey round lamp post, wide base
text: Cylindrical grey lamp posts with a **wide base** are common. Many lamp posts have a white sticker.

images.caption: A grey round lamp post with a wide base; the red circle and arrow point to it

clues.summary: Round grey lamp posts with a wide base. Many have a white sticker.

clues.title: Pole: round wooden poles in rural areas only
text: Utility poles will never be seen in urban rounds, however you might see **cylindrical wooden** poles in rural areas. The poles can be single or double, with electricity counters or transformers attached to them.
clues.summary: No utility poles in cities. In the countryside you may see round wooden poles, single or double, with meters or transformers attached.

clues.title: Guardrail: grey pedestrian rails, no striped kerbs
text: In Hong Kong, you will almost **never** see striped kerbs, which are extremely common in Singapore. In addition, grey pedestrian guardrails are also common.
clues.summary: Striped kerbs are almost never seen, unlike in Singapore where they are extremely common. Grey pedestrian guardrails are common.

differs.how: Singapore has very common striped kerbs

clues.title: Road lines: yellow pedestrian crossings
text: Hong Kong uses **yellow** pedestrian crossings. Some intersections have yellow grids.
clues.summary: Pedestrian crossings are painted yellow, and some junctions have yellow grids.

clues.title: Road lines: white centre, white or yellow edges
text: Hong Kong usually uses **white centre** lines and** white or yellow outer** lines. These lines can be single, double or dashed. Roads are also commonly made of concrete. Yellow outer lines are most commonly found on small roads to indicate no-stopping.
clues.summary: White centre lines with white or yellow edge lines, single, double or dashed. Roads are often concrete. Yellow edge lines on small roads mean no stopping.

clues.title: Sign: white rectangle, thick black border, two languages
text: Road signs are white and rectangular, with a thick black outline and **bilingual **text.
clues.summary: Road signs are white rectangles with a thick black border and text in two languages.

clues.title: Sign: give way, white triangle, thick red border
text: Give way signs feature a white upside down triangle with a **thick red** border and bilingual text.
clues.summary: Give way signs are a white upside-down triangle with a thick red border and text in two languages.

clues.title: Landscape: weathered rock walls with nets
text: Distinct weathered rock walls can be seen on the side of mountains. Some of them have nets, to prevent rockslides. In addition, **green or blue plaques** are a common sight.

images.caption: Circle zooms in on a small green road sign set in a rock wall beside the road

clues.summary: Weathered rock cuts on mountainsides, some covered by nets against rockslides. Green or blue plaques are common.

clues.title: Fire hydrant: red, round top, three outlets
text: Most fire hydrants are red, and usually have **circular tops** and three protrusions. There is also a [pipe-like variant](https://goo.gl/maps/RscuXQ2NrevZ1GDK9). Some fire hydrants have other colours, so make sure to look at their shape or other clues before guessing.

images.caption: Red round-topped fire hydrants with three outlets, seen from two sides

clues.summary: Mostly red hydrants with round tops and three outlets, plus a pipe-like version. Some are other colours, so check the shape.

clues.title: Bollard: yellow with white arrow in blue circle
text: **Yellow **bollards with a white arrow in a blue circle are commonly seen at pedestrian crossings, but also elsewhere, indicating where cars should go. There is a flat and a cuboid version.
clues.summary: Yellow bollards with a white arrow in a blue circle, mostly at pedestrian crossings, showing where cars should go. Flat and box-shaped versions exist.

clues.title: Bins: bright orange on sidewalks
text: Distinct **bright orange** bins can be found on sidewalks.
clues.summary: Bright orange bins stand on sidewalks.

clues.title: Taxi: silver roof, green bumper stickers
text: Hong Kong taxis come in two variants: sedans or station wagons, with the **sedans **most commonly seen. They can be easily identified by their silver roofs, green stickers on the front and rear bumper, and the taxi sign on the roof.

Red taxis are most common on Hong Kong Island and Kowloon, green taxis in the New Territories in the northern region and blue taxis on Lantau Island and Chek Lap Kok. Keep in mind, Hong Kong is a small city and taxis travel all around it.
clues.summary: Mostly sedans, with silver roofs, green stickers on the bumpers and a roof sign. Red taxis are in the central city, green ones in the north, blue ones on the western island, though taxis travel everywhere.

clues.title: Bus: mostly double-decker
text: Buses in Hong Kong are mostly **double-decker**, with various colour schemes and adverts on the side. Single-decker versions do exist, but are less common. Smaller minibuses can also be seen, with a green or red roof.
NOTE: Place names are sometimes visible on the front of the buses, which can be useful for region guessing.
Double-decker buses are also somewhat common in Singapore, but these will often have a recognizable light green colour scheme.
clues.summary: Mostly double-deckers with varied colours and ads; single-deckers are rarer. Minibuses have green or red roofs. Singapore also has double-deckers, usually light green.

differs.how: Singapore's double-deckers are often light green

clues.title: Houses: boxy, a few storeys, in small villages
text: **Boxy **houses that are a few storeys high are a common sight in small villages, mostly to the north of Hong Kong.
clues.summary: Boxy houses a few storeys high in small villages, mostly in the north.

clues.title: Tram: double-decker line on the north of the island
text: A **double-decker** tram line runs along the north of Hong Kong Island. A full map of the route can be seen [here](https://www.travelchinaguide.com/images/map/hongkong/ding-ding-tram.jpg).
NOTE: Make sure not to mistake this tram for the red MTR railway line, which has some sections above ground.
clues.summary: A double-decker tram runs along the north of the main island. Do not mix it up with the red railway, which has some above-ground sections.

clues.title: Train: light rail with green-orange platforms
text: The northwestern part of the New Territories is served by a distinct **light rail system**. It can be recognised by its green-and-orange platforms, single-level train cars and the fact that the tracks are separated from the street.
clues.summary: A light rail with green-and-orange platforms and single-level cars, on tracks separate from the street. It serves the north-west.

clues.title: Houses: crowded gridded streets, flats above shops
text: Mong Kok and the surrounding districts in Kowloon can be recognized by the crowded, **busy, gridded streets**, with apartment blocks situated above the shops.
NOTE: These buildings are usually older, which means there will be a lack of glass walls (as opposed to parts of Hong Kong Island which feature more [glass](https://goo.gl/maps/hJJikEY7wqW8bii48)).
clues.summary: Busy, crowded, gridded streets with apartments above shops. The buildings are older, so few glass walls, unlike parts of the main island.

clues.title: Landscape: flat rice paddies, skyline to the north
text: The north-western area near the Mainland China border is mostly flat and features a patchwork of waterlogged** rice paddies**. The Shenzhen skyline is visible in the distance, to your north.
clues.summary: A mostly flat north-west area with waterlogged rice paddies. A big city skyline appears in the distance to the north.

clues.title: Houses: dense skyscrapers, luxury stores
text: The Central District can be recognized by the large concentration of modern **skyscrapers**. The district feels quite busy, affluent and well-kept, with lots of [luxury brand](https://goo.gl/maps/rxYtmjfiUfxNwYLf6) stores and ads.
clues.summary: Lots of modern skyscrapers, a busy, rich, well-kept feel and many luxury brand shops and ads. It is the central business district.

clues.title: Landmark: two skyscrapers to tell the harbour sides
text: You can use these two **skyscrapers** to determine whether you are on the Kowloon or Hong Kong Island side. The [IFC](https://goo.gl/maps/XaaCZMXmjhrr7h218) is on the Hong Kong Island side and the [ICC](https://goo.gl/maps/my7YFP77nUDga9MD7) is on the Kowloon side.
The ICC has straighter edges and looks more like a cuboid, while the IFC is rounder. The IFC will also have noticeable vertical window frames, while the ICC has none.

images.caption: Two Hong Kong skyscrapers labelled IFC (left) and ICC (right), used to tell the harbour sides apart

clues.summary: One tower is on the island side, the other on the mainland side. The mainland-side tower is boxier with no vertical window frames. The island-side tower is rounder with visible vertical frames.

clues.title: Houses: hilly, tall unique apartment towers
text: Mid-Levels is a residential district that is easily recognized by the non-identical tall modern apartments and **hilliness**.
clues.summary: A residential area with hilly streets and tall modern apartment blocks that differ from each other.

clues.title: Houses: identical white and brown blocks
text: The residential district of Quarry Bay has a lot of identical **white and brown** apartment blocks, and tall glass office buildings.
clues.summary: Many identical white and brown apartment blocks and tall glass office buildings.

clues.title: Coverage: big construction and many bridges
text: Chek Lap Kok Island and the Boundary Crossing Facilities can be recognized by the various large scale **construction **works going on in the area. From the outside, it can be identified by the many [**bridges**](https://goo.gl/maps/vXzoCBzixfWrvgTH6)** **that connect other parts of Hong Kong to the two islands.
clues.summary: Large construction works and many bridges connecting other parts of the territory to the two islands.

clues.title: Houses: identical blocks in a wall, palm trees
text: The residential district of Caribbean Coast and Tung Chung has **identical **apartment blocks that face the same direction, almost like a “wall” of buildings. There are a lot of planted palm trees in between and on the side of roads.
clues.summary: Identical apartment blocks all facing the same way like a wall, with lots of planted palms between them and beside the roads.

clues.title: Bridge: suspension, ladder towers, yellow-red rails
text: The Tsing Ma Bridge can be recognized by being the only major **suspension** bridge in Hong Kong. The bridge has two **ladder-like** support towers, and yellow and red guardrails.
clues.summary: The only big suspension bridge. It has two ladder-like towers and yellow and red guardrails.

clues.title: Bridge: cable-stayed, three round towers, yellow paint
text: Ting Kau Bridge, a **cable-stayed** bridge connecting Ting Kau and Tsing Yi, can be identified by the generally **clean asphalt **and newer condition, three **cylindrical** support towers, hangers coming** directly from the towers** themselves, and yellow paint seen in the median and on the outsides.
clues.summary: A newer-looking cable-stayed bridge with clean asphalt, three round towers, cables attached directly to the towers, and yellow paint in the median and edges.

clues.title: Bridge: cable-stayed, no yellow, box guardrail
text: While similar to the Ting Kau Bridge, the cable-stayed Stonecutters Bridge can be identified by the** lack of **yellow paint, and its **box beam guardrail** design, as opposed to the cable design seen on the other two bridges.
clues.summary: Similar to the previous bridge but with no yellow paint and a box-beam guardrail instead of cable-style rails.

clues.title: Road: skylines on both sides, clean
text: Lung Wo Road can be recognized by the Hong Kong Island** skyline to the south** and the Kowloon skyline to the north. The road is also in good condition and the sidewalks are clean.
clues.summary: The island skyline to the south and the mainland skyline to the north, in good condition with clean sidewalks.

clues.title: Road: divided, river on the west, palm median
text: The Tai Chung Kiu Road is a divided road that runs in a north-east direction, and has views of the Shing Mun **River to the west**. The median has palm trees. In addition, a bicycle path runs alongside the road. Further north, [Route 2](https://goo.gl/maps/D1XThCUDTXBLmhhg8) also runs alongside the river, but this road has more lanes.
clues.summary: A divided road heading north-east with a river on the west, palms in the median and a bike path alongside. Further north a similar road with more lanes also follows the river.

clues.title: Road: narrow, dense jungle, no edge lines
text: Fan Kam Road runs in a general north-east direction, and can be recognized by the dense **tropical vegetation** surrounding the road, and sometimes mountains in the background. The road is also quite narrow and does not have any outer lines. Many [small villages](https://goo.gl/maps/9LA3nzaHZdsVzMvm6) branch off of the road, south and north of the country park.
clues.summary: A narrow road with dense tropical vegetation, sometimes mountains behind, and no edge lines. Small villages branch off it.

clues.title: Road: like the narrow jungle road but busier
text: Lam Kam Road is similar to Fan Kam Road, however it runs in a more **east-west** direction. The road should also feel **busier **with more cars driving along the road and more houses on the sides of the road. In addition, the road is usually wider and a [median](https://goo.gl/maps/Yggjz9dCZCderyto9) containing trees can be seen separating sidewalks near the villages.
clues.summary: Similar to the narrow jungle road but runs east-west, is busier with more houses, wider, and has a tree median by the villages.

clues.title: Landmark: shiny cylindrical terminal, triangle windows
text: The Kai Tak Cruise Terminal can mainly be seen from the Eastern Corridor, north of Tsat Tsz Mui, and from the [Kwun Tong bypass ](https://goo.gl/maps/NUCQ531RFTcqLB4t6)south-west of Kwun Tong. The cruise terminal can be recognized by its shiny, cylindrical appearance, with **triangular windows **along the side.
clues.summary: A shiny, cylinder-shaped cruise terminal with triangular windows on the side. Seen from a highway and a bypass in the east.

clues.title: Bridge: very long sea bridge, black-yellow barriers
text: The Hong Kong-Zhuhai-Macao Bridge can be seen from the South Perimeter Road, on Chek Lap Kok Island. Its **length **stretches into the horizon, spanning across the ocean. The road itself can be recognized by the **black and yellow** concrete barriers on either side.
clues.summary: A very long bridge reaching into the horizon over the ocean. The road beside it has black and yellow concrete barriers.

clues.title: Road: divided, palms, teal street lamps
text: The roads going to Disneyland are divided, with palm trees along the side of the road with **teal **coloured street lamps.
clues.summary: Divided roads with palm trees along the side and teal-coloured street lamps. They lead to a theme park.

clues.title: Coverage: car-free islands, narrow streets
text: Between Hong Kong Island and Lantau Island, there are three unique islands: Peng Chau, Cheung Chau and Lamma Island, with **trekker **coverage. These islands can be identified by the **lack of cars**, narrow streets, and rural architecture. Lamma Island is also the hilliest of the three.
clues.summary: Three small islands with walking-backpack coverage: no cars, narrow streets and rural buildings. One of them is the hilliest.

clues.title: Coverage: black guardrail, skyline view, tourists
text: The Lugard Road trekker around Victoria Peak can be recognized by the distinct** black guardrail**, view of the skyline and tourists walking along the path.
clues.summary: A walking path with a distinct black guardrail, a skyline view and tourists. It circles a famous peak.
